clue.text: Ecstatic shout when back support inserted

indicators.note: inserted means one piece is put inside the word for shout

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily

indicators.note: back tells us the word for support is read the other way round

parts.note: aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Someone yells in delight once a lumbar cushion is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AID into DIA, which is 'inserted' into RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ecstatic is glowing with joy, which is what radiant describes.

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for research goes around the colour word

parts.note: RES is a standard abbreviation for research
buff is a pale yellowish-beige colour

explanation.surface: A study looks into pale fabric samples and inspects them.
explanation.definitionFit: To check someone is to snub or repulse them, the sense of rebuffs as a verb.

parts.note: a weed's fluffy seed head that children puff at, counting the puffs to tell the hour

explanation.surface: Instructions for setting a bomb's timer and detonating it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests planting a bomb timer; in fact the plant is a weed whose seed ball is blown to 'tell the time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Children traditionally blow the seed head of this weed, counting puffs to tell the time, hence a plant used as a timer.

clue.text: Agree to prune head of plant

indicators.note: pruning the head of the plant word cuts off its first letter

parts.note: the sallow is a kind of willow tree

explanation.surface: A gardener consents to trimming the top of a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to permit or agree to something.

parts.note: read not as tower blocks but as a raised area of flat ground

explanation.surface: A pointer to where tall apartment blocks stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a raised stretch of level land, literally an elevated flat.

parts.note: a dairy animal in the literal reading; a business line steadily exploited for money in the figurative one

explanation.surface: Describing a dairy animal kept for the money its milk brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A business or product that reliably generates money is exploited, or milked, for revenue.

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of case

parts.note: to reel is to stagger or waver

explanation.surface: A hopeless person's opening move is to dither.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket case' reads as one phrase, but the basket is the definition and case gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket, especially one used by anglers.

indicators.note: demolished means the building of these letters is knocked down and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeking town's pub has been knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritic means devoted to luxury and pleasure of the senses, like the ancient people of Sybaris.

parts.note: a cell is a small group, e.g. of activists
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A band rings a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument of the violin family is a maker of music.

indicators.note: on reverse means the pair of words together are read backwards

parts.note: to draw is to design
to yaw is to veer off course, zigzagging

explanation.surface: An erratic pattern of zigzags on the back of a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reverse' turns the run DRAWYAW backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward means unpredictable or wilful, departing from the regular path.

clue.text: Stale fruit mostly at bottom of bowl

indicators.note: mostly means the fruit word is cut short at its end

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

indicators.note: at bottom of picks the final letter of bowl

explanation.surface: Fruit left mostly uneaten in the bottom of the bowl has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, the figurative sense of stale.

parts.note: not a dish on the table but a paunch on someone who drinks heavily at the pub

explanation.surface: The main dish at a grand meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supper' here is a heavy drinker (one who sups), and his centrepiece is his midriff.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinker develops a paunch in the middle of his body, his centrepiece.

parts.note: free means unoccupied or empty, as a free seat
a wheel is something that revolves

explanation.surface: An unloaded gun discovered by the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without power, as a cyclist does without pedalling.

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady, so these letters stagger into a new order
left out means the letter L, short for left, is dropped

explanation.surface: A drunken prison guard has been excluded from a wine tasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from JAILOR to give JAIOR, and 'Tipsy' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of that name.

parts.note: to skim a book is to thumb through it

indicators.note: 4 points to the fourth letter of the word Chapter

explanation.surface: A reader flicks through the fourth chapter of a business book on economising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter 4' looks like a heading; it means the fourth letter of 'Chapter'.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise, spending as little as possible.

indicators.note: into means the word it is placed inside the medical word for pressing

parts.note: to palpate is to press with the hands, as a doctor examines

explanation.surface: Pushing it into an arrow holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quiver' looks like an arrow case but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is to throb or tremble, to quiver.

indicators.note: somehow means these letters are worked into some other order

explanation.surface: Negotiators have somehow settled what was owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise is to pay off a debt gradually by instalments.

clue.text: Most blue diamonds extracted from second best deposit

indicators.note: deposit means the letters are set down again in a different arrangement
extracted from means the letter for diamonds is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: The saddest gems were mined from the runner-up's seam.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from SECOND BEST to leave SECONBEST, and 'deposit' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means smutty or indecent, so the most blue is the most obscene.

clue.text: In good nick, chief constable detained relative of villain

indicators.note: detained means the officer's letter is held inside the word for being in good condition

parts.note: in good nick is British for in good condition, i.e. sound

indicators.note: chief means take the head letter of constable

explanation.surface: A top policeman locked up a criminal's relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In good nick' looks like being in a smart prison cell ('nick' is British slang for jail); it means in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a villain.

definitions.meaning: to work out is to reason one's way to a conclusion, to deduce
to judge is to decide after weighing the evidence

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean arriving at a decision by reasoning, as one deduces a verdict.

clue.text: Feel anxious carrying through a delicacy

indicators.note: carrying means the word for feel anxious holds the other word inside

parts.note: to care is to feel concern or anxiety
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Someone frets while bringing through a costly treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare (caviar) is salted sturgeon roe, a luxury food.

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken out over the air, so we hear it

parts.note: cashmere is a fine wool fabric

explanation.surface: Cloth transmitted from a contested territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a Himalayan region whose sovereignty is contested by India and Pakistan.

indicators.note: of means the name is made from part of the following phrase

explanation.surface: Who wrote the song about a know-all?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever Dick' is British slang for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of operas such as Aida.

clue.text: Fast at beginning of Ramadan paid off

indicators.note: at beginning of picks the first letter of Ramadan
off means the letters of paid go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fast at the start of Ramadan was rewarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like the Ramadan fast but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means quick or fast.

clue.text: Big game footballer returns to County

indicators.note: returns means the footballer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Pelé was the famous Brazilian footballer
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A star footballer comes back to his county side for a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' sounds like a major match; it is large wild animals hunted on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game means large animals hunted for sport, such as the African elephant.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for cut is read from the bottom

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Tearing up a draft along with documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Exam papers are the tests themselves, so papers here means examinations.

parts.note: to host is to present a show

explanation.surface: Giving someone a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta is a garden plant grown for its leaves and lily-like flowers.

clue.text: Top dog has mountain of food and drink

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
ham is a food
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: The boss enjoys a huge pile of food and beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dominant member of a group, the top dog, is called the alpha male.

indicators.note: about means the letters of the thinker word are moved around

parts.note: a muser is one who muses or thinks

explanation.surface: A philosopher considers what is liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum is the clear watery fluid that separates from blood.

indicators.note: follow means the word for fewer comes after the word for outcome

parts.note: an end is an outcome or result
less means fewer

explanation.surface: Fewer results follow if something is tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless goes on without variation, so it becomes tedious.

clue.text: It may be seen before or after

definitions.text: It may be seen before or after

parts.words: It may be seen before or after
parts.note: a film preview shown before the main feature, or a cart towed behind a car

explanation.surface: A riddle about something visible either ahead or behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A film preview is shown before a feature, while a towed cart follows behind a vehicle.
